name: 温斯顿·丘吉尔

points.place: 英国牛津郡伍德斯托克
points.title: 贵族少年
points.description: 温斯顿·丘吉尔出生于英国贵族家庭，父亲伦道夫·丘吉尔是政治家，母亲珍妮·杰罗姆是美国富商之女。丘吉尔童年时期主要由保姆抚养，与父母关系疏远。他在哈罗公学接受教育，但学业表现平平，尤其对拉丁语和希腊语不感兴趣。这段时期塑造了他独立思考和叛逆的性格，为他日后不拘一格的领导风格奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Winston Churchill was born into an aristocratic British family, with his father Randolph Churchill being a politician and mother Jennie Jerome being the daughter of an American businessman. Churchill was primarily raised by nannies and had a distant relationship with his parents. He was educated at Harrow School but performed poorly academically, particularly in Latin and Greek. This period shaped his independent thinking and rebellious character, laying the foundation for his unconventional leadership style later in life.

points.title: 战地记者
points.description: 丘吉尔从桑赫斯特皇家军事学院毕业后，以骑兵军官身份开始军旅生涯，同时担任《每日纪事报》和《晨邮报》的战地记者。他先后报道了古巴独立战争、印度西北边境的冲突、苏丹的马赫迪战争，并在第二次布尔战争中成为战俘。在南非的战俘经历让他声名鹊起，成功逃脱后成为全国英雄。这段经历不仅锻炼了他的写作能力，也培养了他对军事战略的深刻理解，为他日后成为战时领导人积累了宝贵经验。
points.descriptionEn: After graduating from the Royal Military College Sandhurst, Churchill began his military career as a cavalry officer while simultaneously working as a war correspondent for the Daily Graphic and the Morning Post. He reported on the Cuban War of Independence, conflicts on India's Northwest Frontier, the Mahdist War in Sudan, and became a prisoner of war during the Second Boer War. His POW experience in South Africa made him a national hero after his dramatic escape. This period not only honed his writing skills but also developed his deep understanding of military strategy, accumulating valuable experience for his future role as a wartime leader.

points.title: 政治家生涯
points.description: 丘吉尔当选为保守党议员后开始了漫长的政治生涯。他先后担任贸易委员会主席、内政大臣、海军大臣、陆军大臣和财政大臣等重要职位。在第一次世界大战期间，他担任海军大臣，提出达达尼尔海峡计划，但遭遇失败。战间期，他反对印度自治和印度宪法改革，同时警告纳粹德国的威胁。1924年他重返保守党，并在1930年代成为少数反对绥靖政策的政治家之一。这一时期，他撰写了大量历史著作，包括《世界危机》和《马尔博罗公爵的生平》，展现了卓越的文学才华。
points.descriptionEn: After being elected as a Conservative MP, Churchill began his lengthy political career, serving as President of the Board of Trade, Home Secretary, First Lord of the Admiralty, Secretary of State for War, and Chancellor of the Exchequer. During World War I, as First Lord of the Admiralty, he proposed the Dardanelles Campaign, which ended in failure. In the interwar period, he opposed Indian home rule and constitutional reforms while warning of the Nazi threat. He rejoined the Conservative Party in 1924 and became one of the few politicians opposing appeasement policies in the 1930s. During this time, he wrote numerous historical works including 'The World Crisis' and 'Marlborough: His Life and Times', demonstrating his remarkable literary talent.

points.title: 战时首相
points.description: 第二次世界大战爆发后，丘吉尔再次出任海军大臣。1940年5月，张伯伦辞职后，丘吉尔组建联合政府并出任首相。面对纳粹德国的侵略，他发表了著名的'我们将战斗到底'演讲，鼓舞了英国人民的抵抗意志。他领导英国在敦刻尔克大撤退后坚持抵抗，与美国建立特殊关系，与苏联结盟对抗纳粹。他高度重视情报工作，支持破译德国密码的'超级计划'。1945年战争结束后，丘吉尔在大选中意外落败，但这段时期确立了他在英国历史上的不朽地位，被誉为'英国最伟大的战时领袖'。
points.descriptionEn: After the outbreak of World War II, Churchill again served as First Lord of the Admiralty. In May 1940, following Neville Chamberlain's resignation, Churchill formed a coalition government and became Prime Minister. Facing Nazi aggression, he delivered his famous 'We shall fight on the beaches' speech, boosting British morale. He led Britain's resistance after the Dunkirk evacuation, established a special relationship with the United States, and allied with the Soviet Union against Nazi Germany. He emphasized intelligence work, supporting the Ultra program for breaking German codes. After the war ended in 1945, Churchill surprisingly lost the general election, but this period secured his immortal place in British history as 'the greatest wartime leader in British history'.

points.place: 英国肯特郡查特韦尔庄园
points.title: 野居岁月
points.description: 丘吉尔在1945年大选失败后成为反对党领袖。这一时期，他主要在肯特郡的查特韦尔庄园度过，专注于写作和绘画。他撰写了《第二次世界大战回忆录》，这部作品为他赢得了1953年的诺贝尔文学奖。同时，他密切关注国际局势，发表了著名的'铁幕演说'，标志着冷战时期的开始。尽管在野，他仍然保持着巨大的政治影响力，为1951年重新执政奠定了基础。查特韦尔庄园不仅是他的居所，也是他思考和创作的重要场所，体现了丘吉尔多才多艺的一面。
points.descriptionEn: After losing the 1945 election, Churchill became Leader of the Opposition. During this period, he mainly spent time at Chartwell in Kent, focusing on writing and painting. He wrote 'The Second World War', which earned him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953. Meanwhile, he closely followed international developments and delivered his famous 'Iron Curtain' speech, marking the beginning of the Cold War. Despite being out of power, he maintained significant political influence, laying the groundwork for his return to government in 1951. Chartwell was not only his home but also an important place for his thinking and creativity, reflecting Churchill's multifaceted talents.

points.title: 再度执政
points.description: 1951年，77岁的丘吉尔再次出任首相，但健康状况已大不如前。他的第二个首相任期主要关注外交事务，包括处理冷战局势、推动欧洲一体化和维持英美特殊关系。1955年，他因健康原因辞去首相职务，但仍保留议员身份直至1964年。退休后，他继续写作和发表演讲，关注国际事务。1965年1月24日，丘吉尔在伦敦逝世，享年90岁。他的国葬是英国历史上最盛大的国葬之一，吸引了全球各国领导人的参加。丘吉尔的逝世标志着一个时代的结束，但他留下的政治遗产和领导风格至今仍影响着英国乃至世界政治。
points.descriptionEn: In 1951, at the age of 77, Churchill became Prime Minister again, though his health had significantly declined. His second premiership focused primarily on foreign affairs, including handling the Cold War, promoting European integration, and maintaining the special relationship with the United States. In 1955, he resigned due to health issues but remained an MP until 1964. After retirement, he continued writing and speaking on international affairs. On January 24, 1965, Churchill died in London at the age of 90. His state funeral was one of the largest in British history, attended by world leaders. Churchill's death marked the end of an era, but his political legacy and leadership style continue to influence British and world politics to this day.

supporter.zh: 丘吉尔被视为英国历史上最伟大的战时领袖和民族英雄。他在二战期间展现出的坚定意志、雄辩口才和非凡领导力，帮助英国在最黑暗的时刻挺住了纳粹德国的进攻。他不仅是杰出的政治家，还是多产的作家和演说家，其作品和演讲激励了无数人。丘吉尔捍卫民主自由、反对极权的立场，使他成为西方世界抵抗暴政的象征。他的远见卓识和战略眼光，为战后世界秩序的建立奠定了基础。
supporter.en: Churchill is regarded as one of Britain's greatest wartime leaders and national heroes. His unwavering will, eloquence, and extraordinary leadership during WWII helped Britain withstand Nazi Germany's darkest hours. He was not only an outstanding statesman but also a prolific writer and speaker whose works and speeches have inspired countless people. Churchill's stance in defending democracy and freedom against totalitarianism made him a symbol of resistance to tyranny in the Western world. His foresight and strategic vision laid the foundation for the post-war world order.

critic.zh: 丘吉尔的政策也面临诸多批评。他在印度问题上的强硬立场导致数百万印度人遭受饥荒；他反对印度独立和自治的立场被视为殖民主义的顽固维护者。在战间期，他对苏联的敌对态度加剧了冷战紧张局势。此外，他的经济政策常被批评为忽视社会公平，对工人阶级权益关注不足。丘吉尔性格中的固执和冲动也导致了一些决策失误，如加里波利战役的失败。这些批评者认为，丘吉尔的光辉形象掩盖了其政策中的争议性和历史局限性。
critic.en: Churchill's policies have faced significant criticism. His hardline stance on India led to famine for millions of Indians; his opposition to Indian independence and home rule is seen as stubborn defense of colonialism. In the interwar period, his hostile attitude toward the Soviet Union exacerbated Cold War tensions. Additionally, his economic policies are often criticized for neglecting social fairness and insufficient attention to workers' rights. Churchill's stubborn and impulsive nature also led to policy mistakes such as the Gallipoli campaign failure. Critics argue that Churchill's glorious image obscures the controversies and historical limitations in his policies.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，丘吉尔被复杂而多面地定义。他既是二战英雄，也是争议性政治人物；既是雄辩的演说家，也是固执的决策者。历史学者强调他在关键时刻的领导作用，同时也客观分析其政策的双重影响。流行文化中，丘吉尔的形象经常被简化为'V'字手势和'我们将战斗到底'的演讲，成为英国坚韧精神的象征。他的名言'我没什么可以奉献，只有热血、辛劳、眼泪和汗水'已成为激励世人的经典。丘吉尔的一生体现了个人意志与历史洪流的交织，他的遗产既有辉煌也有争议，构成了现代世界历史的重要篇章。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Churchill is defined in complex and multifaceted ways. He is both a WWII hero and a controversial political figure; both an eloquent speaker and a stubborn decision-maker. Historians emphasize his leadership at critical moments while objectively analyzing the dual impact of his policies. In popular culture, Churchill's image is often simplified to the 'V' sign and his 'We shall fight on the beaches' speech, becoming a symbol of British resilience. His famous quote 'I have nothing to offer but blood, toil, tears and sweat' has inspired generations worldwide. Churchill's life embodies the interplay between individual will and historical currents, with his legacy containing both glory and controversy, constituting an important chapter in modern world history.

self.zh: 成功不是终点，失败也非末日，最重要的是继续前进的勇气。
self.en: Success is not final, failure is not fatal: it is the courage to continue that counts.

others.zh: 丘吉尔是20世纪最伟大的政治家，他不仅拯救了英国，也拯救了西方文明。
others.en: Churchill was the greatest statesman of the 20th century; he not only saved Britain but also Western civilization.

othersByEn: John F. Kennedy, President of the United States
